item.title: Naitasiri leads Skipper Cup points table after round 5
item.description: Naitasiri is currently leading the Skipper Cup points table after five rounds with 21 points. They have won four and lost one match this season.
item.content:encoded:
Naitasiri is currently leading the Skipper Cup points table after five rounds with 21 points.

They have won four and lost one match this season.

Defending Skipper Cup champions, Malolo are currently in fourth place, with four wins and one loss.

Nadi and Tailevu are level on 20 points, but points difference has placed Nadi in second, with Tailevu in third.

Rewa, who remain winless this season, will be looking to register their first win when they take on Tailevu at Nakelo Ground this weekend.

In the Under-20 competition, Suva tops the standings, with Ba closely behind in second place.

In the Subrails Marama Cup, defending champions Namosi remain at the top of the table with 25 points, followed by Nadi and Suva.

Ba and Rewa continue to search for their first wins of the season.

With the competition progressing, all teams will be looking to improve their performances, build momentum and strengthen their positions in the coming rounds.

Naitasiri faces Taveuni at Cakobau Park this Saturday.

In other matches, Tailevu will take on Rewa at Nakelo District School Ground, while Nadi faces Navosa at King Charles Park, Suva faces Kadavu in Nasese Suva.

In Lautoka, the home side will meet Malolo, while Nadroga takes on Ba at Lawaqa Park,with all games games set to start at 3pm this Saturday.

item.title: Junior Bula Boys thrash Vanuatu 7-2 in OFC U-19 Men’s Championship opener
item.description: The Junior Bula Boys have made a flying start to their campaign after producing a dominant second-half performance to beat Vanuatu 7-2. The two sides were locked 1-all at halftime after an evenly contested opening 45 minutes, before Fiji came alive in the second half and took control of the match.
item.content:encoded:
The Junior Bula Boys have made a flying start to their campaign after producing a dominant second-half performance to beat Vanuatu 7-2.

The two sides were locked 1-all at halftime after an evenly contested opening 45 minutes, before Fiji came alive in the second half and took control of the match.

Abudullah Khairati, Jovesa Uqe, Ibraheem Afzal, Ryan Naresh and Nicholas Franklin were among the goal scorers for Fiji.

Franklin put the finishing touch on Fiji’s impressive performance by scoring the final goal and was also named Player of the Match.

The result gives coach Marika Rodu and his Junior Bula Boys the perfect start to their campaign, with their second-half performance particularly impressive after Vanuatu had matched them in the first half.

Attention now turns to a much bigger test, with Fiji taking on New Zealand this Saturday at 4pm.

The stakes are high in the tournament, with the winner and runner-up qualifying for the FIFA U-20 World Cup 2027 in Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan.

item.title: Suva bounces back as Tupou shapes young Skipper Cup Side
item.description: For Tupou, the challenge has not only been about results but also about helping a group of young players adjust to the demands and intensity of provincial rugby. He says many of his players have performed strongly at club level, but the Skipper Cup has presented them with a different challenge.
item.content:encoded:
For Tupou, the challenge has not only been about results but also about helping a group of young players adjust to the demands and intensity of provincial rugby.

He says many of his players have performed strongly at club level, but the Skipper Cup has presented them with a different challenge.

The coach believes the experience of playing against some of the best provincial sides in the country is helping his young players develop both physically and mentally.

Their win last week has also provided a timely boost as Suva looks to build some momentum heading into the second half of the competition.

Tupou says the focus now is on maintaining that improvement and ensuring the players learn from each match.

With Kadavu standing in their way in Round 6, the coach says Suva will be looking to carry the confidence from last week's victory into another important encounter.

Suva will meet Kadavu at Nasese ground this Saturday at 3pm.

In other matches, Tailevu will take on Rewa at Nakelo District School Ground, while Nadi faces Navosa at King Charles Park.

In Lautoka, the home side will meet Malolo, while Nadroga takes on Ba at Lawaqa Park, Naitasiri faces Taveuni at Cakobau Park with all games games set to start at 3pm this Saturday.

item.title: Enzo Fernandez set for Manchester City move as City agree £125m fee with Chelsea
item.description: Manchester City have agreed to pay a joint-British record transfer fee of £125 million ( FJD $371 million ) for Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez. The two clubs have been negotiating over the past 24 hours and have now reached an agreement for the 25-year-old Argentina international.
item.content:encoded:
Manchester City have agreed to pay a joint-British record transfer fee of £125 million ( FJD $371 million ) for Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez.

The two clubs have been negotiating over the past 24 hours and have now reached an agreement for the 25-year-old Argentina international.

Fernandez will undergo a medical before signing a long-term deal with City, with personal terms not expected to be an issue.

He joined Chelsea from Benfica in 2023 for a then-British record £107 million ( FJD $318 million ).

Chelsea had hoped to keep Fernandez earlier this summer, but the midfielder had been pushing to leave the club since March.

Fernandez had been targeting a move to Real Madrid, but the Spanish club later ruled out making an offer.

This is the second time City have broken their own transfer record this summer after signing Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for £116 million (FJD $345 million).

Fernandez will also become the fourth player to move to a Premier League club for at least £100 million (FJD $297 million) this summer.

item.title: Fiji U-19 begin OFC Championship campaign against Vanuatu
item.description: The Fiji Under-19 football team will begin their OFC U-19 Men’s Championship 2026 campaign against Vanuatu in Samoa today. Coach Marika Rodu says he is thrilled with his side’s preparation and believes the squad has plenty of experience heading into the tournament.
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji Under-19 football team will begin their OFC U-19 Men’s Championship 2026 campaign against Vanuatu in Samoa today.

Coach Marika Rodu says he is thrilled with his side’s preparation and believes the squad has plenty of experience heading into the tournament.

The team completed a six-week training camp at the Fiji Football Academy in Ba and played training matches against OFC Men’s Champions League teams Lae City FC and AS Tiga Sport ahead of the tournament.

Rodu says seven players in the squad featured at the last FIFA U-17 World Cup, while two players are returning for their second U-19 competition.

He says four players have OFC Pro League experience with Bula FC, while nine players are based overseas.

The coach says their goal is to qualify for next year’s FIFA U-20 World Cup.

Fiji are in Group B alongside defending champions New Zealand, Tahiti and Vanuatu.

Fiji will face Vanuatu at 10am today before taking on New Zealand at 2pm on Saturday.

Their final pool match will be against Tahiti at 10am next Tuesday.

The winner and runner-up of the tournament will qualify for the FIFA U-20 World Cup 2027 in Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan.

item.title: David Ellis appointed Interim Defence Coach of Flying Fijians
item.description: David Ellis has been appointed as the interim Defence Coach of the FIJI Water Flying Fijians for the upcoming Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup in September . The Fiji Rugby Union s ays Ellis is currently in camp with the Flying Fijians and has begun working alongside the national coaching staff and players as preparations continue for the tournament.
item.content:encoded:
David Ellis has been appointed as the interim Defence Coach of the FIJI Water Flying Fijians for the upcoming Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup in September .

The Fiji Rugby Union s ays Ellis is currently in camp with the Flying Fijians and has begun working alongside the national coaching staff and players as preparations continue for the tournament.

They say the British coach brings more than 25 years of coaching experience at the highest levels of international and professional rugby, specializing in defensive systems and player development.

FRU says his CV records involvement in more than 1,000 professional club matches and more than 200 Test matches during his coaching career.

FRU says Ellis is particularly well known for his long association with the French national team, where he served as Assistant Defence Coach from 2000 to 2011. They say during that period, France won multiple Six Nations titles, including Grand Slams, reached Rugby World Cup semi-finals in 2003 and 2007, and progressed to the 2011 Rugby World Cup Final, where they were narrowly defeated 8–7 by New Zealand.

FRU adds that his international experience also includes working as a coaching consultant with the New Zealand All Blacks during their 3–0 Test series victory over the British & Irish Lions in 2005, as well as defence coaching roles with Tonga and Romania and consultancy work with USA Rugby Sevens.

More recently, Ellis was Defence Coach with Romania during its 2023 Rugby World Cup qualification campaign and helped the side secure a bronze medal in the 2023 Rugby Europe Championship.

Romania’s campaign included victories over Poland, Belgium and Spain, culminating in the bronze-medal result.

FRU says at club level, Ellis has worked extensively in England and France with teams including Gloucester, Castres Olympique, CA Brive, London Irish and Lyon. His time with Lyon included Pro D2 championship successes in 2014 and 2016. His later coaching record includes guiding Kenilworth RFC to the RFU Intermediate Cup at Twickenham in 2019, coaching Sarlat Rugby to 22 wins from 22 matches and promotion from Federale 2, and coaching Bletchley Rugby Club to the BBO Premier League title after winning 19 of 20 matches and conceding just 81 points across the season.

Ellis has also served as a World Rugby Coach Development Mentor, sharing his defensive expertise and experience with international coaches.

His immediate focus with the FIJI Water Flying Fijians will be on strengthening the team’s defensive systems and working with the wider coaching group as the squad builds towards its Pacific Nations Cup campaign .

The Flying Fijians are currently in camp preparing for the competition, with Ellis already actively involved in the team’s preparations.

Fiji plays Canada in the opening match of the Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup next Saturday at 7pm, which also serves as the semi-final of the competition.

item.title: Erasmus makes four changes for third All Blacks test
Taveuni rugby draws strength from Vanua support ahead of Skipper Cup Round 6
item.description: Mikaele Liga , Navitalai Naivalurua · 01/09/2026 The Taveuni Rugby team is gearing up for a physical battle when it travels to Nausori this weekend to meet Naitasiri in Round 6 of the Skipper Cup Competition.
item.content:encoded:
Mikaele Liga , Navitalai Naivalurua · 01/09/2026

The Taveuni Rugby team is gearing up for a physical battle when it travels to Nausori this weekend to meet Naitasiri in Round 6 of the Skipper Cup Competition.

The team will be drawing strength from the support of the Vanua as it continues its campaign in the competition.

Taveuni is a newcomer to the Skipper Cup and has defied expectations throughout the season.

They narrowly lost 24-23 to defending champions Malolo in Round 1 before going down 28-18 to Navosa in Round 2.

Their first win came in Round 3, when they defeated Ba 27-25, followed by a historic 32-22 victory over Nadroga in Round 4.

Last week, Taveuni went down fighting against Nadi, losing 24-13.

The club says the team is made up largely of farmers from the island, with players having to balance their commitments at home with training, travelling and preparing for competitive rugby.

It says the continued support and blessings of the Vanua remain a major source of strength as the players navigate the demands of a long rugby season.

As the season progresses, the club says supporters on Taveuni and on the mainland have stepped up to ensure the players are well looked after, particularly with meals, rugby equipment and other necessities.

Fans who spoke with fijivillage Sports say their support is driven by their belief in the players and their desire to see Taveuni continue competing strongly in the Skipper Cup.

They say fundraising efforts are ongoing to help provide food and rugby gear for the team.

S upporters also visit the players’ camp to encourage them and show their appreciation for the sacrifices they are making.

The club says support from the Vanua extends beyond financial assistance, with traditional blessings, encouragement and regular camp visits providing additional motivation for the players.

Taveuni will face Naitasiri at 4pm at Ratu Cakobau Park this Saturday.

In other matches, Tailevu will take on Rewa at Nakelo District School Ground, while Nadi faces Navosa at King Charles Park.

In Lautoka, the home side will meet Malolo, while Nadroga takes on Ba at Lawaqa Park.

A ll matches are scheduled for 3pm this Saturday.
